page: Microsoft Azure B16als_v2 is a burstable general purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical execution cores with hyperthreading enabled at a rated frequency of 3.525 GHz. The configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance does not include bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data requirements.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, with stress-ng single-core achieving 2703.69 and PassMark memory performance reaching 2808.57, both ranking in the top 25 percentile. Multithreaded performance aligns within the middle 50 percentile, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng rating of 21607.66, a PassMark CPU metric of 22213.52, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9731.0. Memory throughput reaches 131.85 GB/sec on large block reads, supporting 16.54 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.62 GB/sec in static web serving tests.

The 1:2 memory-to-core profile provides high computational thread density while avoiding excess memory resource allocation. Because CPU execution is governed by a burstable allocation model, long periods of full saturation will deplete credit reserves, representing a key operational tradeoff compared to dedicated vCPU offerings. The instance is suited for batch processing, intermittent software compilation, CI/CD build runners, and web services with fluctuating traffic patterns.
